text:
maria: FYI we're getting a spike of duplicate 'resume' sessions from mobile clients after the sticky-lease TTL change. Console shows 2 active sessions for the same resume-id and billing reports double token counts. :grimacing:

alex: ugh, saw this on canary too. repro steps?

maria: quickly — client disconnects (cell -> wifi switch), reconnects with same resume-id. Proxy routes to a different edge because old lease expired between disconnect and reconnect (~35s). Both edges accept resume and start separate KV caches.

sam: so both edges think they own the session and both consume tokens? that'd explain billing dupes. :eyes:

alex: can you paste the headers from the reconnect attempt? especially resume id and lease header

maria: pasted below from the mobile repro run:
```
GET /sse/stream?id=abc123 HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
x-resume-id: rsm-7f4a
x-session-lease: 2024-11-03T12:01:02Z
User-Agent: RedwoodMobile/1.4.12
```

jordan: deploy-bot: canary proxy-v2.8 deployed to us-east-1 at 2024-11-03T12:02Z

alex: timeline looks like: lease TTL changed to 30s in proxy-v2.8, clients with flaky networks get >30s pause, reconnect goes to new proxy; old proxy didn't immediately revoke resume token so it still resumed locally. Race causes two active streams.

sam: options: 1) make resume id global (persist resume ownership to central store), 2) extend sticky-lease TTL, 3) enforce single-accept at control plane with idempotency check and immediate revoke on accept.

maria: 1 and 3 need infra work. 2 is fastest but we still risk duplication if network blips > TTL. ops-bot: what's current quota/billing protection?

ops-bot: current billing dedupe window = 2s per token-group; resume duplicates are outside that window.

alex: console-bot, can the dashboard hide resumed duplicates if they reappear within X seconds? we'd like UX to not confuse SREs and customers while infra fix lands.

console-bot: we can add a 'merged-session' view that groups sessions by resume-id and shows combined token usage. That would be a backfill UX in ~3d if approved.

jordan: engineering tradeoff: merging on UI masks the real backend duplication — ops might miss billing alerts. But it's a reasonable interim.

sam: long-term I'd push for an idempotent accept path at the control plane: accept-resume should be a single-writer operation with Compare-And-Set on resume-id -> owner mapping and immediate revocation RPC to previous owner (if any). That prevents two edges from both running KV caches.

maria: agree. short-term mitigation: bump sticky lease to 90s on proxy-canary for mobile-heavy regions and add a resume-accept timeout: once a proxy accepts resume, it writes accept to Redis with 1s TTL; another accept reading that key must delay and verify origin. Might avoid dupe spawns.

alex: also add telemetry: emit resume_accept_attempt with fields {resume_id, proxy_id, accepted_bool, conflict_bool, latency_ms}. we don't currently have conflict metrics. :+1:

maria: adding that will help quantify. also request: console should expose a per-tenant 'resume_conflict_rate' metric so support can correlate billing spikes to conflict events.

jordan: can we throttle token billing for sessions flagged as 'resume_conflict' until we verify which session is correct? We risk undercharging though. Finance? (cc @finance)

sam: risky. instead mark tokens from conflicting sessions as 'probation' in billing pipeline and surface them separately — don't immediately bill until conflict resolves. That needs a billing pipeline change though.

maria: immediate action items:
- bump sticky-lease TTL to 90s on mobile-regions canary (jordan)
- add resume_accept conflict telemetry (alex)
- console: grouped session view & resume_conflict_rate (console-bot)
- infra: design idempotent accept + owner mapping RFC (sam/maria)

alex: I'll own the telemetry PR. Will add the event schema and a quick Grafana dashboard query.

console-bot: created ticket CONS-4212 for grouped-session UI and CONS-4213 for exposing resume_conflict_rate (ETA 72h).

jordan: rolling TTL bump to canary now. monitor: resume_conflict_rate, token dupes, console grouped-sessions.

maria: thanks. i'll follow up with sample logs from 3 customers. if anyone sees unexpected billing spikes, ping me directly. :pray:
